text:
sam: merged cust-verdant/lora-tax into staging @main. used q4_0 globally but kept lm_head fp16. kicking off verdant-quickpack now.
lee: heads up — finetune added token <TAXCODE> via added_tokens during training but tokenizer file wasn't updated in repo. might split.
prio: training logs looked clean, but we did an extra epoch on sparse invoice samples. hoping for better tax-code extraction.
eval-bot: QuickEval: verdant-quickpack finished on staging@verdant-lora-q4
  summary: 74/88 checks passed, 14 flagged, 1 flaky parse failure
  regressions: tax_code extraction F1 down 3.4% (baseline 94.0 -> 90.6)
  hotspots: <TAXCODE> token split, tax-rate normalization, negative-tax handling, small uptick in hallucinated tax notes
  artifacts: s3://redwood/artifacts/verdant/1776543210/quickpack-report.html
sam: can you paste a repro snippet?
lee: repro (sanitized):
```
OCR: "Line item: Service - taxable
Tax: <TAXCODE>-TX-07
Amount: $150.00"
Expected: {"tax_code":"TX-07","tax_amount":"15.00"}
Model: tax_code:"T X - 0 7", tax_amount:"15 . 00", note:"token: < TAXCODE >"
```
prio: token splitting + quantized attention probabilities seem to insert spaces. lm_head fp16 helped but not sufficient.
sam: eval-bot says rollback threshold for verdant invoice pipeline = 2.5% F1 drop. we're at 3.4%  blocking deploy.
prio: immediate mitigations:
  1) runtime postproc remap: collapse ['<','TAXCODE','>'] -> '<TAXCODE>' and remove whitespace in tokenized numeric groups (fast)
  2) re-run quickpack with mixed export keeping attention/kv fp16 and rest q4_0 (to test if attention quantization is amplifying punctuation probs)
  3) add exact-match tax_code canonicalization test to quickpack so future runs gate faster
lee: I can patch the quickpack tests and add the runtime remap. sam can you try mixed export?
sam: starting mixed-quant export: keep attention/lm_head fp16, rest q4_0. will run on ded-cluster-4, ETA ~12m.
perf-bot: scheduled perf probe with 200 streams, 50 warmup tokens; will report p50/p95 lat and tokens/sec after run.
eval-bot: note: quickpack also includes a bias/regression check for customer-specific tax rules (important for compliance). flagged 6 samples with differing tax-rate normalization.
ops-bot: created ticket ML-4872: "verdant lora tax_code regression" assigned to sam. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-4872
prio: decision rule: if mixed-quant reduces F1 drop below 1.5% we can do 1% canary with Console monitors; if not, rollback and plan token addition to tokenizer + fusion train.
sam: mixed-quant run finished:
  quickpack summary: 81/90 checks passed, 9 flagged
  tax_code F1 delta: -0.9% (baseline 94.0 -> 93.1)
  tax-rate normalization fixed on most samples, hallucinated note regressions reduced
  perf: p50 token latency +8%, p95 +12%, tokens/sec -7% (acceptable for canary)
lee: nice. runtime remap + mixed-quant looks good. still add tokenizer change later for long-term fix.
prio: schedule 1% traffic canary with automatic rollback if Console detects >1.5% F1 degradation on tax pipeline. add monitoring hook for hallucinated-tax-note metric.
sam: deploying 1% canary now and updating ticket with artifacts + perf numbers. :eyes:
ops-bot: updated ML-4872 with artifacts and canary plan.
prio: thanks team. follow-up: plan token addition + light fusion retrain next sprint, and add explicit tax-code canonicalization postproc in customer adapter.
